title: Cardinality of the disjointness fooling set
statement: For every $n \in \bbn$, the fooling set for disjointness — the collection of all pairs $(X, X^c)$ with $X \subseteq [n]$ — has exactly $2^n$ elements.
replaced:
The fooling set $\mathrm{foolingSet}(n)$ has cardinality $2^n$, since it is in
bijection with the power set of $[n]$ via $X \mapsto (X, X^c)$.
